name: Comments
description: A conversation on the instance: messages, each top-level or a reply in the thread of a top-level one, one level deep, which their authors edit and delete, others react to and pin, and whose threads are resolved and reopened. A message may be streamed as it is written: begin holds its place as composing, appendDraft adds to its draft and sends the draft signal to the streams open on the instance, and finish posts it; one whose author stops appending for composeTimeoutMs is interrupted, keeping what was written. Readers send typing and viewing, signals the engine delivers and does not keep. Each caller has a read marker on the conversation and on each thread, which markRead moves, and follows the threads it posts in, is mentioned in, or follows with follow. Each message that comes to stand, and each edit that adds a mention, records a delivery for each subject it mentions and each follower of its thread but its author, which a notifier or an agent dispatcher outside the engine claims and settles with claimDeliveries and settleDeliveries; the engine sends nothing. inbox reads a caller's mentions, followed threads and read conversations across every schema of the namespace it may read. Every writing operation on an instance is beside the instance: it writes Comments' own tables, never moves the instance's seq, ETag or updatedAt, and runs none of its guards, so a lease on the instance does not stop a reply. A caller who may read the instance reads the conversation; the policy is asked write for a writing operation, post included. Deleting the instance deletes its conversation, with its read markers, follows and deliveries.

blocks.description: The block kinds a post, an edit or a finish may give; every kind when absent, none when empty.

composeTimeoutMs.description: How long a composing message's author may append nothing before the engine's runner interrupts it, in milliseconds; 60000 when absent. The runner looks for such messages every quarter of it, or every 15 seconds when that is sooner.

deliverPermission.description: The permission a notifier or an agent dispatcher needs to claim and settle the deliveries of this type's messages, beside the policy's Comments.claimDeliveries and Comments.settleDeliveries. Absent, nobody claims them, and they serve only the inbox.

deliveryRetentionMs.description: How long a delivery is kept from when it was made, in milliseconds, whatever its state but a live claim; the inbox's mentions reach back as far. 2592000000, 30 days, when absent.

editWindowMs.description: How long after a message's postedAt its author may edit it, in milliseconds; no limit when absent. A caller holding moderatePermission is not held to it.

maxAttempts.description: How many times a delivery is claimed before a failure, or a claim that lapses, drops it; 5 when absent.

maxBodyLength.description: The longest body a post, an edit or a finish may give, and the longest draft appendDraft builds, in code points; 40000 when absent.

maxDrafts.description: The most composing messages one subject may have on an instance at once; begin refuses another. 5 when absent.

moderatePermission.description: The permission that lets a caller edit, delete and interrupt another's message, edit past editWindowMs, and purge. Absent, only a message's author edits, deletes or interrupts it before composeTimeoutMs passes, and nobody purges.

pinPermission.description: The permission a caller needs to pin and unpin. Absent, any caller the policy lets write may.

resolvePermission.description: The permission that lets a caller resolve and reopen another's thread. Absent, only a thread's author does.

retryBackoffMs.description: How long after its first failure a delivery is due again, in milliseconds, doubled after each later failure up to an hour; 30000 when absent.

fields.name: messages
fields.description: How many posted and interrupted messages the conversation has, top-level and replies; composing, deleted and purged ones are not counted.

fields.name: lastMessageAt
fields.description: The greatest postedAt of a posted or interrupted message, in epoch milliseconds; absent while there is none.

fields.name: threads
fields.description: The posted and interrupted top-level messages, each a thread, whether resolved or not: { open, resolved }.

fields.name: composing
fields.description: The subjects writing a message now: each subject with a composing message on the instance, once, in the order of its earliest composing message's id; empty while nobody is.

fields.name: unread
fields.description: The caller's: how many posted and interrupted top-level messages of others came to stand after the caller's read marker on the conversation. 0 until the caller first reads the conversation with markRead or posts in it top-level, so a conversation nobody opened is unread for nobody. Replies are read thread by thread, in the inbox, and not counted here.

operations.name: post
operations.description: Posts a message as the caller: top-level, or a reply in the thread of a top-level message, which may quote a message of that thread. A composing message has no thread to reply in and cannot be quoted. A ref block's instance must be one the caller may read, and each block's kind one the config allows. A retry with the clientId of a message the caller posted or began returns that message and posts nothing.

blocks.description: Structured parts beside the body, each of a kind the config allows.

items.description: A block, checked against its kind.

oneOf.description: Another instance of the namespace, which the poster must be able to read when the block is posted; a reader's own read decides whether it opens.
A card for something the poster did, "ran the tests" say; an edit moves its status.

data.description: What a client shows with it, at most 8192 bytes as compact JSON.

body.description: The text, Markdown, at most the config's maxBodyLength code points.

clientId.description: The caller's key for the message, so a retry returns the message it posted.

mentions.description: The subjects the message names for someone to hear of it: a person's, an agent's or a group's (role:<name>), as the client resolved them from what was typed.

quotes.description: The id of the message of the thread the reply quotes, the top-level one or a reply; needs thread.

thread.description: The id of the top-level message to reply in; a top-level message when absent.

author.description: The subject of the caller who posted or began it.

items.description: A block as it was posted: ref { kind, schema, id }, or action { kind, title, status, data? }.

body.description: The text, Markdown: the draft so far while composing; empty once deleted.

participants.description: On a top-level message: the subjects that have a posted or interrupted message in its thread, the top-level one included, the one whose latest such message is latest first, at most 10.

mine.description: Whether the caller reacted with the emoji.

replies.description: On a top-level message: how many posted or interrupted replies its thread has.

resolved.description: On a top-level message whose thread is resolved: who resolved it and when.

stand.description: The message's place in the order the conversation's messages came to stand: 1, 2, 3, ... on the instance, given when it is posted, finished or interrupted and never changed. operations.name: begin
operations.description: Begins a message as the caller, composing: it takes its id and its place in the conversation now, top-level or a reply in the thread of a top-level message, which may quote a message of that thread, and shows the caller as writing. Its author adds the text with appendDraft and posts it with finish; one whose author appends nothing for the config's composeTimeoutMs is interrupted. Nothing is counted until it is finished or interrupted. A caller may have at most the config's maxDrafts composing messages on the instance. A retry with the clientId of a message the caller posted or began returns that message and begins nothing.

operations.name: appendDraft
operations.description: Appends text to the draft of the caller's composing message, and once the call commits sends the draft signal, { message, offset, text }, to the streams open on the instance. A reader that opens the conversation midway reads the draft so far as the message's body and follows the signals from its length. Its author only; the draft holds at most the config's maxBodyLength code points. An empty text appends nothing and sends nothing, and still counts as an append, so an author at work with nothing to show keeps its message from being interrupted. It appends no event.

message.description: The id of the composing message.

text.description: The text to append, at most 4000 bytes written as a JSON string, its quotes included, so that the draft signal fits a signal's 4096 bytes.

length.description: The draft's length after the append, in code points.

offset.description: The draft's length before the append, in code points: where the text starts.

operations.name: finish
operations.description: Posts the caller's composing message: its body is body, or the draft when body is absent, checked as a post's body is, and its blocks and mentions are as a post gives them. Its author only. The message keeps its id, its place and the createdAt its begin gave it, and is counted from now.

operations.name: interrupt
operations.description: Stops a composing message: it becomes interrupted, its draft its body, or deleted when its draft holds no text. Its author may at any time, and so may a caller holding moderatePermission; any caller the policy lets write may once the author has appended nothing for the config's composeTimeoutMs, which is how the engine's runner interrupts a message whose author has stopped, on its schedule. An interrupted message is counted from now.

operations.name: markRead
operations.description: Moves the caller's read marker past the messages it has read: on the conversation's top-level messages, or with thread on that thread's replies. upTo is the greatest message id the caller has shown; every posted or interrupted message of the listing with an id up to it is read, and a streamed reply that comes to stand later is not. The marker never moves back. Only the caller reads it back, so it appends no event, and a caller who may read the instance may call it.

thread.description: The id of a top-level message: the marker moved is the caller's on its thread's replies, whether the caller follows it or not. The conversation's when absent.

upTo.description: The greatest id of the messages read: a bound, which need not name a message.

resultSchema.description: The caller's marker after the call.

readUpTo.description: The marker: the greatest stand of the messages read; 0 when none is.

unread.description: How many posted or interrupted messages of others in the listing stand above the marker.

operations.name: follow
operations.description: Follows a thread, so each reply that comes to stand in it records a delivery for the caller and the inbox lists it, or with on false stops. A caller follows each thread it posts in and each it is mentioned in without asking, again after it stopped. Following counts the thread's replies from the latest message of the conversation. Only the caller reads it back, so it appends no event, and a caller who may read the instance may call it.

on.description: true to follow, false to stop.

thread.description: The id of the thread's top-level message.

following.description: Whether the caller follows it now.

thread.description: The id of the thread's top-level message.

operations.name: listMessages
operations.description: Lists a page of the conversation's top-level messages, or with thread a page of that thread's replies, composing and deleted ones included, a composing one with its draft so far as its body, in ascending id order: the latest page when no anchor is given, the page before or after a message id, or the page around a message of the listing. Each page says where the next older and newer ones start.

after.description: The page is the earliest messages with a higher id.

around.description: A message of the listing: the page holds it and the messages either side of it. At most one of around, before and after.

before.description: The page is the latest messages with a lower id.

limit.description: At most this many messages; 50 when absent.

thread.description: The id of a top-level message: the page is its thread's replies, and the result carries the message as root.

after.description: The id to pass as after for the page of newer messages: the last item's, when the listing has a newer message; null when it has none or the page is empty.

before.description: The id to pass as before for the page of older messages: the first item's, when the listing has an older message; null when it has none or the page is empty.

operations.description: Lists what a message held before each of its edits, oldest first, one page at a time.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

limit.description: At most this many edits; 50 when absent.

blocks.description: The blocks before the edit.

items.description: A block as it was posted: ref { kind, schema, id }, or action { kind, title, status, data? }.

body.description: The body before the edit.

by.description: The subject of the caller who made the edit.

edit.description: The edit's number on the message: 1, 2, 3, ...

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: listReactions
operations.description: Lists who reacted to a message with an emoji, in the order they reacted, one page at a time.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

emoji.description: The reaction: an emoji's name or the character itself, at most 32 code points.

limit.description: At most this many reactions; 50 when absent.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who reacted.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: inbox
operations.description: The caller's inbox across every schema of the namespace that composes Comments and that the caller may read, newest first: the messages that mention it, the threads it follows that have replies of others, and the conversations it has read that have top-level messages of others. Each item names the latest such message and how many of them the caller has not read; an item with none unread is done. A mention is read once the caller's marker on the conversation, for a top-level message, or on its thread, for a reply, passes it. Mentions reach back as far as the config's deliveryRetentionMs.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

kinds.description: The kinds of item to list; every kind when absent.

limit.description: At most this many items; 50 when absent.

unread.description: true lists only items with unread messages, false only done ones; both when absent.

excerpt.description: The message's body with each run of white space made one space, at most 200 code points, ending with an ellipsis when cut.

kind.description: mention, a message that mentions the caller; thread, a thread the caller follows, by its latest reply of another; conversation, a conversation the caller has read, by its latest top-level message of another.

message.description: The id of the message the item shows.

postedAt.description: When the message came to stand, in epoch milliseconds: the item's place in the inbox.

thread.description: The id of the thread's top-level message, when the message is a reply; on a thread item, the thread followed.

unread.description: On a mention, 1 while the caller has not read the message and 0 after; on a thread or a conversation, how many messages of others stand above the caller's marker. 0 makes the item done.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

operations.name: claimDeliveries
operations.description: Claims deliveries that are due, at most limit, oldest due first, under one new token that lapses after ttlMs, so two notifiers never send one twice: each pending one, each failed one whose next attempt has come, and each claimed one whose claim lapsed. Only deliveries of schemas the caller may read whose config names a deliverPermission the caller holds; with subjects or prefix, only theirs. A due delivery whose message no longer stands, or whose subject has read it, is dropped and not returned. Each delivery carries what a notifier needs to act with no other read.

limit.description: At most this many deliveries; 20 when absent.

prefix.description: Only deliveries to subjects that start with it, agent: say; not with subjects.

ttlMs.description: How long the claim holds, in milliseconds; 60000 when absent. A delivery not settled by then is due again.

expiresAt.description: When the claim lapses, in epoch milliseconds; null when nothing was claimed.

attempt.description: Which claim of the delivery this is: 1 for the first.

body.description: The message's body as it is now, Markdown, at most its first 4000 code points.

id.description: The delivery's id, which settleDeliveries takes: opaque, and the same at each claim.

postedAt.description: When the message came to stand, in epoch milliseconds.

reasons.description: Why: mention, the message mentions the subject; reply, the subject follows the thread. Both, in that order, when both hold.

state.description: The message's: posted, or interrupted when its author stopped before finishing it.

subject.description: Who should hear of it: a person's, an agent's or a group's (role:<name>) subject, as the message gave it; a notifier expands a group.

thread.description: The id of the thread's top-level message, when the message is a reply.

via.description: The deployable of the service whose call posted or began the message (D37).

token.description: The claim's token, which settleDeliveries takes; null when nothing was claimed.

operations.name: settleDeliveries
operations.description: Settles deliveries the caller claimed under token: sent; failed, which makes each due again after a backoff until the config's maxAttempts claims, then drops it; or dropped. Needs the deliverPermission of each delivery's schema. Every id must be held under the token, or nothing is settled.

error.description: Why it failed or was dropped, kept on the delivery; not with sent.

ids.description: The ids of the deliveries to settle.

items.description: Each delivery, in the order of ids.

attempts.description: How many times it has been claimed.

nextAttemptAt.description: When a failed one is due again, in epoch milliseconds.

state.description: sent, failed or dropped: a failure on its last attempt is dropped.

signals.name: typing
signals.description: The sender is typing a message: top-level, or with thread a reply in that thread. A client sends it every few seconds while its person types, and a reader shows the sender as typing for a few seconds after the last; the engine keeps none. Comments does not check that thread names a message.

thread.description: The id of the top-level message whose thread the sender is typing in; absent for a top-level message.

signals.name: viewing
signals.description: The sender has the conversation open. A client sends it every few seconds while it shows the conversation, and a reader shows the sender as looking for a few seconds after the last; the engine keeps none.

signals.name: draft
signals.description: Text appendDraft added to a composing message's draft, sent once its call commits; from is the message's author. A reader that holds offset code points of the draft appends text; one that holds fewer missed a signal and reads the message again with getMessage; one that holds more ignores it.

message.description: The id of the composing message.

offset.description: The draft's length before the text, in code points.

vetoes.description: The id a call names, as message, thread, quotes or around, is not a message of the conversation, or a purged one; or around names a message outside the listing. details: message.
thread names a reply, not a top-level message: post, begin, listMessages, resolve, reopen, markRead and follow. details: message, thread, the reply's thread.
post or begin with quotes naming a message outside the thread it replies in. details: message, thread.
An edit, delete, reaction, pin, resolve or reopen of a deleted message, or a post or begin quoting one. details: message.
An edit, reaction, pin, resolve or reopen of a composing message, a post or begin replying in the thread of a composing top-level message, or quoting a composing message. details: message.
appendDraft, finish or interrupt of a message that is posted, interrupted or deleted. details: message, state.

An edit or delete of another's message, or a resolve or reopen of another's thread, by a caller without moderatePermission (resolvePermission for a thread); or appendDraft or finish of another's composing message, which nobody but its author writes. details: message, author.
An edit by the message's author more than the config's editWindowMs after its postedAt. details: message, postedAt, editWindowMs.
An edit of a message that has been edited 500 times. details: message, max.
react with an emoji the caller has already given the message. details: message, emoji.
unreact of an emoji the caller has not given the message. details: message, emoji.
react with a 21st distinct emoji on a message. details: message, max.
pin of a pinned message. details: message.
unpin of a message that is not pinned. details: message.
resolve of a resolved thread. details: thread, by, at.
reopen of a thread that is not resolved. details: thread.
A block of a kind the config's blocks does not list. details: block, its index in blocks; kind; allowed.
A ref block whose instance does not exist or the caller may not read, the same refusal for both. details: block, schema, id.

interrupt of another's composing message, by a caller without moderatePermission, whose author appended less than the config's composeTimeoutMs ago. details: message, author, lastAppendAt, composeTimeoutMs.
begin by a caller that has the config's maxDrafts composing messages on the instance already. details: composing, how many it has; max.
appendDraft whose text would make the draft longer than the config's maxBodyLength. details: message, length, append, maxBodyLength.

purge on a type whose config names no moderatePermission; or claimDeliveries or settleDeliveries in a namespace none of whose schemas the caller may read names a deliverPermission. details: permission, "moderatePermission" or "deliverPermission".

settleDeliveries with ids that name no delivery of a schema the caller may read and whose deliverPermission it holds: never made, pruned, or removed with its message or its instance. details: ids, those ids, in the order given.
settleDeliveries with a token no delivery holds now: each it claimed has been settled, or claimed again after the claim lapsed. details: token.
settleDeliveries with ids of deliveries that do not hold the token: pending, settled, or claimed under another token after this claim lapsed. details: token; ids, those ids, in the order given.
